description: Offline authentication triage with traceable evidence.
input: Path to a regular UTF-8 file.
output: Create a new report file; never overwrite.
input_format: Input grammar: jsonl or ssh (default: jsonl).
burst_threshold: Failures per account to trigger AL-001 (default: 5).
max_line_bytes: Maximum bytes per line including newline (default: 16384).
year: Explicit year for traditional SSH timestamps.
timezone: Fixed UTC offset for traditional logs, e.g. --timezone=-03:00.
strict: Stop at the first malformed record.
fail_on: Exit 1 for findings at or above this severity.
log_file: Create a new structured lifecycle log without identities.
quiet: Suppress informational diagnostics; keep reports and errors.
no_color: Disable colors (text output is already plain).
err_usage: Invalid arguments. Use --help to review flags, choices and required values.
err_config: Invalid configuration. Check key names, types and limits in docs/configuration.md.
err_language: Unsupported language. Select en, es, ru or zh-CN.
err_io: Cannot read input/configuration. Provide a readable regular file, not a link or directory.
err_output: Cannot create output/log. Choose a new filename in a writable directory; existing files are never overwritten.
err_limit: Input limit exceeded. Split the export or deliberately adjust documented limits.
err_record: Malformed or unsupported authentication record. Check the input schema and line diagnostics.
err_encoding: Invalid UTF-8. Export the file as UTF-8 before analysis.
err_legacy_time: Traditional SSH timestamps require --year and --timezone; use ISO timestamps for mixed years.
err_legacy_order: Traditional timestamps went backwards. Use an immutable export with explicit ISO dates; no year rollover is inferred.
err_input_changed: Input changed during reading. Retry with an immutable copy.
partial: Input is incomplete or has no analyzable events. Review quality counts and diagnostics.
report_notice: Indicators require human investigation. They do not establish malicious intent or compromise.
no_findings: No indicators matched. This does not prove the input or environment is safe.
observation_text: {events} events across {accounts} account(s), from {start} to {end} UTC.
AL-001.title: Repeated authentication failures
AL-001.inference: Failure volume meets the configured per-account threshold. Password guessing is plausible, not confirmed.
AL-001.hypothesis: Determine whether the source represents unauthorized attempts or a legitimate client with stale credentials.
AL-001.recommendation: Review source ownership, user activity and adjacent authentication/endpoint logs before taking action.
AL-001.false_positive: User retries, stale automation credentials and misconfigured clients can produce the same pattern.
AL-002.title: Failures across multiple accounts
AL-002.inference: Account breadth meets the configured threshold and is compatible with password spraying. Attempted passwords are unknown.
AL-002.hypothesis: Determine whether one source is probing multiple accounts; shared source addresses may represent many legitimate users.
AL-002.recommendation: Check NAT/proxy context, authorized testing windows and identity-provider logs; do not infer password reuse from these records.
AL-002.false_positive: Shared NAT, QA tests, authentication outages and broken SSO clients can affect many accounts together.
AL-003.title: Successful login following repeated failures
AL-003.inference: A success follows threshold-reaching failures for the same account and source. Access occurred; unauthorized access is not established.
AL-003.hypothesis: Determine whether this was legitimate recovery or access obtained after repeated attempts.
AL-003.recommendation: Verify with the account owner and inspect the resulting session and endpoint activity. Preserve evidence before containment.
AL-003.false_positive: A user correcting a password or an administrator fixing a client can legitimately succeed after failures.
